chunks: Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ali al-Asadi told us, saying: My father, Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Bajali, and al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn al-Nasr al-Tusi told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghazwan told us, saying: Abu Sinan al-Abidi told us, saying: Safwan ibn Sulaym narrated from Ataa' ibn Bashir, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:
The carriers of the Qur'an are the consciously knowing ones from the people of Paradise.

key_terms.عُرَفَاءُ: Consciously knowing ones / Those with deep intuitive knowledge

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of those who memorize the Qur'an according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, this hadith from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri elevates the *huffaz* (memorizers) to the rank of *'urafa*, implying they possess the intuitive discernment and spiritual insight characteristic of the elite of Paradise. This designation underscores the Shia scholarly view that Qur'anic preservation is not merely mechanical recitation but a transformative act that cultivates deep gnosis (*ma'rifah*) and prepares the soul for eternal proximity to the Divine. The term *'urafa* here links the physical burden of the text with the metaphysical reality of being among the 'knowers' who navigate the realms of the afterlife with clarity.
